title: The reshimu and the Kav: the Essence that makes the rules and can break them
overview:
The last chapter's analogies now meet their *nimshal*. After the *tzimtzum* G-d left a *reshimu*, an impression that holds His whole *etzem*, but as a *hiyuli*, a point that could become anything, and so in itself it shows nothing: a tree is a tree, a rock is a rock, ink is ink. He is seen through the *Kav*, His choice imposing an order, as a soul is seen in the movements of a body and a squirrel's forgotten acorns plant the forest.

The *Kav* holds two opposites. It unites everything, even *chesed* in the vessel of *gevura*, and it is the *kav hamida* that measures every light and vessel. Both are true, because it comes from the *Atzmus*, and whoever makes the rules can break them: the teacher with his class plan, the architect with his blueprint, the husband who can change the pool room. So every change, from weekday to *Shabbos* and from the *Beis HaMikdash* to *galus*, comes from the Essence, and we pray to Him, not to His *middos*. Two Q and A tapes bring it down to squirrels, coffee, nerves and cells.

sections.title: The reshimu: everything hidden in a point, so the world looks separate
sections.summary: The *reshimu* left after the *tzimtzum* holds G-d's whole *etzem*, but as a *hiyuli* that could become anything, so in itself it reveals nothing and the world looks separate from Him. He is seen only through the *Kav*: His choice, the order and the changes He imposes, as a soul is seen in the movements of a body.

phrases.he: (טו) והנמשל מכל הנזכר לעיל
phrases.en: Now the analogue, the real point of everything that we said until now,

phrases.he: יובן בבחינת רושם
phrases.en: it's understood about the impression.

phrases.he: שנשאר בחלל ומקום פנוי הנזכר לעיל

blocks.text:
**Now the analogue, the real point of everything that we said until now**: really just of the last chapter, which asked how a *Kav* (the line of light) can come out of the *reshimu* (the impression left after the *tzimtzum*). A *reshimu* is complete *helem* (concealment); a *Kav* is *gilui* (revelation).

They are not opposites: put points together and you get a line. A point is a *koach hahiyuli* (raw potential), the essence everything is built from. It has no *gilui* and no *hispashtus* (spreading forth) not because it cannot reveal, but because it could reveal anything.

So the *nimshal* (what the analogy stands for): G-d makes a *tzimtzum* (contraction) by way of *siluk* (removal), hiding His *or* (light), that is, hiding His *etzem* (essence). What is left looks separate from Him: just *osios* (letters).

That is the *chalal reikan* and *makom panui* (an empty space, a vacant place): a potential for something to appear separate from Him, holding the form of everything G-d could make, seen as separate. That is **the impression**.
Practically for us: when you look at the world and do not see its connection to G-d, so that it seems a collection of isolated points, you are seeing only the *reshimu*.

phrases.he: (שהוא יו"ד דס"ג
phrases.en: this *reshimu* is the *yud* of the name *SaG*

phrases.he: שבטהירו עילאה כמו שכתוב בספר עמק המלך)

blocks.title: The yud of SaG
blocks.text:
A kabbalistic digression, hence the parentheses: **this reshimu is the yud of the name SaG** (the Name of sixty-three). Spell out *SaG*, and the last *yud*, the one in its last *hei*, is the *reshimu*.

First G-d made the *tzimtzum* round: the *siluk* of the light that is *b'li gvul* (without limit). The other part of the *tzimtzum* is a *miut* (lessening) of the limited light: *olam hamalbush*, the world of the garment, a square *makif* (encompassing light), root of the *tallis*, the *sukka* and everything square. In the *makom panui* G-d made the *hashara* (estimation) of everything He could make, a square woven of letters, root of *memalei kol almin*, with the Names *Ayin Beis*, *SaG*, *MaH* and *BaN* in its corners.

blocks.title: Folding the square of letters
blocks.text: Then G-d folded the square over onto itself, and each letter, paired with another, was hidden: *MaH* with *Ayin Beis*, *BaN* with *SaG*. But *BaN* has only nine letters and the others ten, so the last *yud* of *SaG* had no pair and was left sticking out. That *yud* is the *reshimu*.

blocks.title: From the middle to the top
blocks.text:
So there are really two *reshimus*. The round *tzimtzum* leaves a *roshem* in the middle of the *chalal*; G-d blew it up into the square, folded it, and left this *yud*, another *nekuda* (point), at the corner touching the circle. The *Kav* starts from there.

Rabbi Walters always wondered how the point left in the middle got to the top, where the *Kav* comes from. This is how.

blocks.title: To one side
blocks.text: It also explains *Tanya*, chapter 45 he thinks, where G-d was *metzamtzem* (contracted) His light *l'tzad echad*, to one side. Why one side, if a circle is all around? Because there it means the square *tzimtzum*, folded over to one side. The square comes up later, with *bina* (understanding). So much for the kabbalistic digression.

phrases.he: שהוא בחינת היולי כולל כל מה שיסתעף ממנו על ידי הקו וחוט כו'
phrases.en: this *roshem* is a *hiyuli* that includes everything that's going to come out from it in the *Kav*

blocks.text:
**This roshem is a hiyuli that includes everything that's going to come out from it in the Kav.** What comes out in the *Kav* is nothing new, only the *gilui* of particulars already hidden in the *reshimu*.

As with the teacher: all his knowledge is hidden in his memory, a *roshem*, and each explanation he brings out is a little *Kav*. Like points that can make any shape, the *osios* he knows can be arranged in infinite ways; that is why it is a *hiyuli*.

phrases.he: וגם שנתעלם כללות האור העצמות
phrases.en: but even though the general *or* of the *Atzmus* was hidden by the *tzimtzum*,

phrases.he: עד שלא נשאר רק בחינת רשימו,
phrases.en: until only an impression was left,

phrases.he: עם כל זה ודאי הכל נכלל בו בקיצור
phrases.en: even though it's only *reshimu*, surely everything is hidden there in a short way,

phrases.he: על ידי זה הצמצום דווקא
phrases.en: through this very *tzimtzum*,

phrases.he: כנזכר לעיל

blocks.text:
**But even though the general or of the Atzmus was hidden by the tzimtzum**, **until only an impression was left**: the point of the *tzimtzum* is that the *osios* can be handed to a student, independent of the teacher's mind. Before it, the letters of his knowledge are one thing with his mind. Now he makes the information as if independent of him, so he can just tell you the facts and you do not have to be him. The knowledge is still in there, but it seems separate.

So too G-d makes the world look separate, but really it is *mamash* (actually) G-d Himself, the *Atzmus*.

The *tzimtzum* is not *kipshuto* (literal), and it is not a place: really everything is G-d, as before it. The only question is how it looks separate. G-d is *kol yachol* (all-capable): He can show you what it would be like if He were not there, and He can be in a limited way. The point is not that things look different, since you could see different things and still see G-d, but that you no longer see them as connected to Him. That is what G-d wanted.

blocks.title: The soul seen in the body's movements
blocks.text:
How then do you see the connection? Through the *Kav*, which is like His *bechira* (choice): from the fact that He changes things, departs from the order, you see there is a G-d there.

So with the body: the soul's control reveals the person, though the body is no soul at all; the movements show an intellect, an emotion. Look at the body at any one second and it is a dead, physical thing, and the next second too. That is why time is the intermediary between *olam* (world) and *nefesh* (soul): the soul is revealed through the changes.

So too the G-dliness in the world, a *ratzon* (will), an intellect, you see mainly in the changes over time, in everything being run with a purpose; and even in one moment, in the contrast between things.

First you see it as separate: a tree is a tree, a squirrel is a squirrel, an isolated point. But once you see a tree you already see a *Kav*: roots, trunk, branches, infinite points put in a certain form, and from the differentiations you see an intellect and a purpose. The more you put together, the more you see.

blocks.title: The squirrel that forgets its acorns
blocks.text: Then you see the symbiosis of trees, animals and bugs. Rabbi Walters once watched a squirrel burying an acorn in a little hole, the way they officially hide them for after the winter. But they do not remember where they put them, so it cannot be for themselves. G-d *davka* (specifically) makes them want to hide them, and then they forget, so that they plant the trees: "they work for the tree."

blocks.title: G-d's cleanup crew
blocks.text: All the bugs and bacteria in the world are little workers with their jobs. When there are crumbs on his floor and the ants come for them, it is as if G-d sends a little cleanup crew to take the leftover food away and turn it into something useful.

**Even though it's only reshimu, surely everything is hidden there in a short way**, **through this very tzimtzum**: the *tzimtzum* stuffs everything into the *reshimu* by way of *kitzur* (shortening); it does not take it away.

G-d is *metzamtzem* Himself: He decided that He is going to be a squirrel. It is *mamash* Him, His whole *etzem*; you just do not see it.

blocks.title: He's hurting this piece of meat
blocks.text: Like the soul in the body. On the one hand the body is *mamash* you: that is why you get angry when someone hurts it, and you would not accept that he is only hurting a piece of meat. On the other hand it is not you: nothing a person does to your body can kill, hurt or maim the soul.

So too with G-d, only in one direction: He is not *mamash nitfas* (caught). He decided to become a squirrel but was not trapped into one. He is higher than any form, and that is why He can reveal Himself in any form.
Compared with that, the great unknowable beyond is pretty lame: "I know some squirrels that are better than that."

So He is not stuck in it, and that is why bowing to a thing is *avoda zara* (idol worship). It is Him the way your body is you: you, only when you realize you are something higher, though you are *mamash* in your body. And since the *tzimtzum* is not *kipshuto*, the whole *gilui* of the *Atzmus* is in the *reshimu*, and the *Kav* can come out of it: in the *koach hagvul* (the power of limit), G-d is revealed as He transcends all forms.

blocks.question: Why talk about squirrels and trees, things of *Asiya*, when the subject is a high spiritual level before even *Atzilus*?
blocks.text: Not cosmic vibrations of supernal energies in the essential quintessence of everything, which nobody knows the meaning of. Everything in the *hishtalshelus* (the chain of descent) is here in front of us. G-d Himself is sitting with us, we are staring Him in the face and do not know it; we get a full *gilui* of the *Atzmus Ein Sof* before the *tzimtzum* and do not realize it. The point of learning this is to see "where is the *Atzmus Ein Sof* in my coffee?" That is *hashgacha pratis* (Divine providence).

blocks.text: True, the *Kav* and *reshimu* come before the world was created and are not the example he gives; but the example still comes from them. Like language: first a concept, then a representation, letters. The concept of a letter exists before the ABCs and before ink on paper; yet all the way down the *hishtalshelus*, this *alef* on the paper is a letter. So the *reshimu* is G-d's ability to reveal a particular form.
blocks.outOfPlace: From the Q and A tape on chapter 15 (class 47), which reads no line: a student's question on class 40's squirrels and trees, answered with the reshimu of line 4.

blocks.text:
G-d is *kol yachol*: if He wants to be a butterfly, He can be a butterfly. Before the *tzimtzum* we realize He is choosing it, so you see the whole *Atzmus* in whatever He chooses, and to Him it is all the same. The *reshimu* is that He hides Himself and reveals all the options as if separate from Him.

Everything below comes through the *reshimu*, so everything has a *reshimu*-ness: the source of the *keilim* (vessels), of its seeming separate, limited and defined. Whenever we see something as just a point, its own entity, that is the *reshimu*, even in an example from *Asiya*.
blocks.outOfPlace: From the Q and A tape on chapter 15 (class 47), which reads no line: a student's question on class 40's squirrels and trees, answered with the reshimu of line 4.

blocks.text: Of the Mitteler Rebbe's five *meshalim* (analogies) for the *reshimu*, only throwing a stone is a *mashal* for the *reshimu* itself. The other four, the *Mishna* to the *Gemara*, the blueprint, the mnemonic and the hand motion, are, as the Rebbe Rashab explains in *Ayin Beis*, *meshalim* for how it is revealed in each world of *ABYA*. The general *inyan* (concept) of the *reshimu* is that something looks separate from G-d, as if He were no longer involved: maybe it came from Him, but now it is separate.
blocks.outOfPlace: From the Q and A tape on chapter 15 (class 47), which reads no line: a student's question on class 40's squirrels and trees, answered with the reshimu of line 4.

blocks.text: The squirrel is not the *reshimu* part. That anything appears separate and distant from G-d, thrown, is the *reshimu* of it, and you don't need a squirrel for that. The *reshimu* is the *gilui* of G-d's power of *gvul* (limit) seen as separate from His power of *b'li gvul*.
blocks.outOfPlace: From the Q and A tape on chapter 15 (class 47), which reads no line: a student's question on class 40's squirrels and trees, answered with the reshimu of line 4.

blocks.question: And the teacher teaching a student: where is the *reshimu* there?
blocks.text:
It is the teacher's ability to turn his information into *osios*, as if the knowledge were separate from his mind. Ideas do not really exist outside the mind, but we make them as if they do; that is *osios*. It is his memory, the *reshimu*: ideas filed away like letters without being consciously thought, though really they are always thought in a hidden way, or he would forget them.

Making a *tzimtzum* and leaving a *reshimu* is clearing your mind, putting everything in memory and leaving the conscious mind blank, a *chalal reikan* and *makom panui*. Now you can bring up the *osios* by way of a *Kav*, to the student.
blocks.outOfPlace: From the Q and A tape on chapter 15 (class 47), which reads no line: a student's question on class 40's squirrels and trees, answered with the reshimu of line 4.

blocks.text: G-d wanted the world to look separate, so that we should have to work to see Him. You do not see Him so much in the thing; you see Him in the *Kav*, in the changes He makes, His *bechira*. That is what the chapter mainly explains: all the changes in the *hishtalshelus* are controlled only by G-d. As the body needs the soul to tell it what to do, the *bechira* comes straight down to your little pinky toe, and everything in the middle changes nothing.

blocks.title: Brain, nerves and the moving object
blocks.text: *Tanya* recently spoke of the *Kav*, the *haara* (glow) of the *Kav*, and the *haara* of the *haara*. Your essential *bechira* goes only into your brain, your consciousness, and from there through the nerves to the organs; were the nerves, G-d forbid, cut, the person would choose and the body would not respond. Then the arm throws or moves a thing, so when you see the thing move, though it is separate, you see the effect of the choice made in the brain.
blocks.outOfPlace: From the second Q and A tape on chapter 15 (class 48), which reads no line: it goes on from class 47 about how G-d is seen in the Kav, the subject of class 40 on line 4.

blocks.text: So the light of the *Kav* itself is only in the brain; its *haara* goes through the nerves to the body, which is like the *keilim* of *Atzilus*, still connected. What you write, say or make is only a *haara* of your choice, yet a *bekia* (breaking through) of the *masach* (screen): you see the person in what he does. So we see G-d not in the things, which seem limited, but in action: He controls everything and chooses how it should be.
blocks.outOfPlace: From the second Q and A tape on chapter 15 (class 48), which reads no line: it goes on from class 47 about how G-d is seen in the Kav, the subject of class 40 on line 4.

blocks.text: As a soul fills the body, so G-d fills the world: the *Midrash* on *Barchi nafshi es Hashem*. It is one of the *meshalim* for the *tzimtzum*: the *etzem* of the soul stays higher than the body, yet comes down, connects to it and controls it, and you see the soul in the body. So there is a *tzimtzum*, but not *kipshuto*: you see *hashgacha*, choices, G-d changing things.

phrases.he: וגם מה שהוא מורה העדר ההתפשטות למטה,
phrases.en: but there's another problem: the *reshimu* is in a way that it's not *mispashet*.

phrases.he: אינו בחינת צמצום גמור
phrases.en: it's not a complete *tzimtzum*, that G-d is preventing us from seeing Him.

phrases.he: רק מצד שהוא בחינת כח ההיולי כו'
phrases.en: That's because it's in a way of *koach hiyuli*.

phrases.he: כנזכר לעיל

blocks.text: **But there's another problem: the reshimu is in a way that it's not mispashet.** Everything was stuffed in so short that there is no *hispashtus*, just a point, nothing to pull the G-dliness out by. The *Mishna* at least talks about the same thing as the *Gemara*, so you have something to work with: a little that contains a lot.

blocks.title: The rock and the bad guy's pit
blocks.text: Had G-d just created a rock floating there, never changing, you would never figure out any higher reality from it. It is like the video games where you jump across platforms that fall after a second: you always wonder why the bad guy did not simply make one big pit. With only the *reshimu*, G-d would stick us here with nothing to work with: "All we know is the rock."

So how can we be expected to find G-d, if the world is a *reshimu*, thrown and separate, with no apparent meaning? Even so, **it's not a complete tzimtzum, that G-d is preventing us from seeing Him**.

That nothing in the physical world, or anywhere in the *hishtalshelus*, looked at in isolation, lets you draw a conclusion is **because it's in a way of koach hiyuli**: it has the power to reveal G-d's whole *etzem*, so you could make anything of it. Until you compare it to something else, you have no reference.

blocks.title: One word on a piece of paper
blocks.text: A person isolated in the world could come up with all kinds of explanations of reality; things on their own give no clue to their meaning. Hand someone a paper with one word of a foreign language, say *Michal*, and he will never figure it out: not because the letters stop him, but because they are *hiyuli*. The same letters could mean something else.

So too G-d could use the same creations to reveal anything. That certain things reveal certain aspects of Him and others other *middos* (attributes) He set up afterward, from the *Kav*. You cannot force a person looking at the world to admit anything, because one level of reality is just an essential existence you could attach anything to.

blocks.title: Ink on paper
blocks.text: Looking only at the ink on the paper, you cannot prove that *v'hanimshal* reads as it does, or that the *vav* is a *vav*. It does not have to be that sound or any sound: "It is ink into this shape, that's what it is." Anything else is an association you bring to it, a whole other layer of reality.

You do not see it there inherently, not because it stops you from making a language, but because it is the essential building block, and anything can be made of it. G-d first created isolated things, then put them in an order and a form that works like a language and reveals. So too your body is set up to reveal your soul, though it did not have to take that form. Why don't you see a person in a calcium molecule? Because it does not have to be a person; it can become part of anything.

phrases.he: רק להיותו כח מגביל לכללות האור הראשון,
phrases.en: since the *reshimu* is this *koach* that limits the whole original light,

phrases.he: על כן בלתי מתפשט רק דרך קו, לפי אופן ההשפעה כנזכר לעיל.
phrases.en: Everything only comes out by way of a *Kav* according to the way that he wants to bring out the *hashpa'a*.

blocks.text: **Since the reshimu is this koach that limits the whole original light**, G-d's whole *etzem* is there, so every single thing just is, because it is. That is the root of the feeling of the *yesh gamur* (the complete, independent something), and what it means that it comes from the *yesh amiti* (the true Existence). That a thing is its own *metzius* (existence), with no cause, purpose or meaning, always was and always will be, needing nothing else, is a *gilui* of G-d's *etzem*. Since He put Himself into every thing, you see that as the most basic level of everything.
So it is revealed only when a *Kav* is made of it: to reveal different things you have to put an order on it, since in itself it could be in any order.

blocks.question: The *reshimu* is a bunch of *osios*, each with the whole *etzem*: is it one thing?
blocks.text: No, the *reshimu* is infinite. Compared to before the *tzimtzum* it is a zero of the *Ein Sof*, less than a single point; but in *osios* it is infinite: all the *osios* of the *hashara*, the *gelaf glifu* (the engraving), without the light. The *reshimu* is basically everything G-d is not, everything that does not look like Him, revealed to Himself.

blocks.title: The teacher's lesson order
blocks.text: The *Kav* brings out only some of the *reshimu*, as the teacher brings out only some explanations: **Everything only comes out by way of a Kav according to the way that he wants to bring out the hashpa'a** (the flow, the teaching). To him there is no *maala u'mata* (higher and lower), so he imposes an order: start here, then that, then this.

So it says of *Chassidus*: it is *igulim* (circles), with no *maala u'mata*, all one point. You cannot truly say this is basic, that advanced, this built on that. Yet it has to be learned in order, first the *seder hishtalshelus* as *Shaar HaYichud* explains it. *Shaar HaYichud* is a *Kav* the Rebbeim imposed; understand it properly and you see it is all the same essential point, expressed in different ways.

sections.title: The Kav carries the infinite light, measured out for the receivers
sections.summary: The *Kav* has in it the light from before the *tzimtzum*, truly infinite, measured out only for the receivers, as a real teacher can explain anything at the student's level. Its order of higher and lower is a help to see G-d, the one who uses wisdom, and then to see His whole *etzem* in every point.

phrases.he: אמנם יובן מהנזכר לעיל דקו זה יש בו מכח האור הראשון שלפני הצמצום
phrases.en: However, from what we said in the last chapter, it's understood that really the *Kav* is not limited.

phrases.he: בבחינת אין סוף ממש,
phrases.en: It could bring out the whole light of before the *tzimtzum*, in a completely infinite way.

phrases.he: רק שבא דרך קו, לפי אופן המקבלים כו'
phrases.en: Just it's coming in a measured way according to the recipients.

blocks.text: **However, from what we said in the last chapter, it's understood that really the Kav is not limited.** **It could bring out the whole light of before the tzimtzum, in a completely infinite way.** Like the teacher explaining in a measured way: if the student is on his level, he can take it all the way back to his own. **Just it's coming in a measured way according to the recipients**: to little ones, in a little way.

His *mashal* of a teacher and student who are *b'erech* (in proportion) means a real teacher, one with the essence of intellect, which almost nobody has. That essence is really *Chassidus*: then you know everything, and it is only a matter of putting it together in different ways; a qualitatively different understanding, not a lot of things learned. There is no time to explain that now.

blocks.title: The posek hador
blocks.text: He knows everything but tells you what you can take. Think of a *posek hador* (the halachic authority of the generation): he knows *halacha* with *omek* (depth), so whatever situation you bring, he never learned it, yet he puts the pieces together and tells you the *halacha* for it. He measures your situation and answers for it; but if you are on the right level, he can go all the way back up and talk to you on his level, where he sees everything.

So within the *Kav* G-d could reveal His whole *etzem*, but He chose the *hishtalshelus*, revealing Himself in a limited way, so each thing seems to have its own *chayus* (life force), its own *gilui*, in a limited system: so that there be *avoda* (divine service) and a world. If He wanted, He could blow it back up and show the whole *koach* of the *Ein Sof* in you, or in a cup of coffee.

phrases.he: ובזה יובן מה שכתוב באורך נראה אור
phrases.en: from Your light we see a different light,

phrases.he: בחינת הארה דהארה
phrases.en: only like a ray of a ray,

phrases.he: הנקרא אור של תולדה
phrases.en: which is called like a born light, meaning that it changes its form.

phrases.he: שאחר הצמצום בוקע האור דרך קו בעלמא כו',
phrases.en: after the *tzimtzum*, the light breaks through, … but it's only coming through the *Kav*.

phrases.he: אבל הוא בא מאורך העצמי
phrases.en: but the light that we're seeing is coming from Your essential light.

phrases.he: להיות שברשימו הרי נכלל הכל
phrases.en: because the whole *etzem* is really hidden in the *reshimu*,

phrases.he: וממנו נמשך הקו
phrases.en: and the *Kav* is coming out from the *reshimu*,

blocks.text: So we understand what is written, **from Your light we see a different light**: **only like a ray of a ray**, **which is called like a born light, meaning that it changes its form**: the *or shel tolda*. The light we see is G-d Himself, but as a light of a light that changes, so it looks like a revelation of *chachma* (wisdom), *Keser* (crown) or *bina*, and then of more particular things: the wisdom of squirrels, a particular *chayus*, a particular truth. In it we see a little reflection of G-d, not the whole picture, and through it a glimpse of the Creator.

**After the tzimtzum, the light breaks through**, a little glimmer of G-d, **but it's only coming through the Kav**, in a measured way. Wisdom as a concept separate from G-d, the vessel of wisdom, comes from the *reshimu*: G-d is not wisdom. But that someone is using the wisdom, executing it in the world, is a *bekia* of the *Atzmus Or Ein Sof*: G-d Himself is doing the wisdom.

blocks.title: Smarter than an apple tree
blocks.text: In the trees, the squirrels, anything, you see a big wisdom. Rabbi Walters does not know how to make apples, and he thinks he is smarter than an apple tree, "cause it's just stupid wood." Spiders did not figure out their webs, and bees, which are not that smart, make honeycombs at perfect angles: G-d put it into them. You see that there is a wise one behind it, someone higher than wisdom using the wisdom.

blocks.title: Hearing a person in the sounds
blocks.text: Talking to you, I hear intelligence in your sounds, and I do not say there is intelligence; I say there is an intelligent person. I see you only through the ways you express yourself, but it is you I see: intelligence is a quality you have, not your *etzem*. So too we realize there is a G-d who uses wisdom and is higher than it. But He comes now only through the ten *sefiros* (the Divine attributes), the *Kav* He measures out, so we see Him through His wisdom, His will, His kindness.

**But the light that we're seeing is coming from Your essential light**: through the limited form it is G-d Himself, **because the whole etzem is really hidden in the reshimu**, **and the Kav is coming out from the reshimu**.

phrases.he: בבחינת היולי לכללות השפע להיות בבחינת מעלה ומטה
phrases.en: The *Kav* is a *hiyuli* to make things in a way of *maala u'mata*.

phrases.he: על כל פנים,
כמו שכתוב בעץ חיים
phrases.en: like it says in *Etz Chaim*.

blocks.text: The *Kav* reveals what is hidden in the *reshimu* only by way of *maala u'mata*, a progression, so you have a way to start: A, then B, slowly working toward G-d. But once the *Kav* helps you *chap* (grasp) G-d, you see Him in the thing itself: every point *mamash* chosen by Him, His whole *etzem* in it. The order was only to bring you to that.

blocks.title: One letter and many letters
blocks.text: A writer puts his *sechel* (intellect) into every single letter; but for you to *chap* that there is a *sechel*, he has to write a lot of letters.

The *etzem or* is hidden in the *reshimu*: every point has the whole *etzem*, but you do not see it, because it is a *hiyuli* and you do not know how to pull it out. So G-d reveals it in a *Kav*, a limited *hamshacha* (drawing down) by way of *maala u'mata*. In a way that is not true: G-d does not insist it be *davka* this way, start here, then there. But going through that *Kav* helps you find the *Atzmus* hidden in the *reshimu*, since the *Kav* is drawn from it.

**The Kav is a hiyuli to make things in a way of maala u'mata.** The *reshimu* is a *hiyuli* for everything; a measuring stick, as the last chapter said, is a *hiyuli* to measure anything. The *Kav* says only that *al kol panim* (at any rate) there will be *maala u'mata*: an order, a form, a start and an end, so you have a way to *chap* it; within that, any order you want. Like explaining an idea in writing: write whatever you want, but it starts here and goes right to left. **Like it says in Etz Chaim.**

sections.title: Two opposites in the Kav: it unites, and it measures
sections.summary: The *Kav* unites all the lights, so that even *chesed* can go into the vessel of *gevura*, and it is also the *kav hamida* that measures every light and vessel and makes the distinctions. That looks like a contradiction, but whoever makes the rules can break the rules.

phrases.he: ומזה הטעם
phrases.en: for this reason

phrases.he: יובן תירוץ על ב' ענינים הפכים שנמצא בקו זה
phrases.en: we can answer the seeming paradox of two things we see in this *Kav* that seem to be opposite things:

phrases.he: הא' אשר בכחו דוקא לאכללא שמאלא בימינא כו'
phrases.en: that the *Kav* can make *hiskalelus* between opposites,

phrases.he: שהוא בחינת ההתכללות והיחודים של כל האורות המסתעפים מכתר דאדם קדמון עד מלכות דאצילות
phrases.en: that the *Kav* is *davka* what makes everything work together.

phrases.he: עד שעל ידו דוקא יוחלף האור בכלי שאינו שלו,
phrases.en: until *davka* from the *Kav*, the light can go into its opposite vessel even,

phrases.he: כמו אור החסד בכלי הגבורה כו'
phrases.en: that you can decide that you're going to express your *chesed* through *gevura*.

phrases.he: כמו שכתוב במקום אחר באריכות בענין וא''ו דוהנורא כו'
phrases.en: like it explains at length in other places, about the *vav* of *v'hanora*

blocks.text: **For this reason** **we can answer the seeming paradox of two things we see in this Kav that seem to be opposite things.** The first: **that the Kav can make hiskalelus between opposites** (inclusion of one in the other), showing that two opposites are really one. **The Kav is davka what makes everything work together**, all the lights from *Keser* of *Adam Kadmon* to *Malchus* (kingship) of *Atzilus*. As in a person: all his *ratzonos* (wills) and powers work together because he controls them by conscious choice, and you see one person using them.

**Until davka from the Kav, the light can go into its opposite vessel even**, like the light of *chesed* (kindness) in the vessel of *gevura* (might, restraint): **you can decide that you're going to express your chesed through gevura**, being nice to a person by being strict. You are not a machine, stuck in a system: you have free choice.

**Like it explains at length in other places, about the vav of v'hanora.** In *Shemoneh Esreh*, *hagadol* is *chesed*, *hagibor* is *gevura*, and *hanora* is *tiferes*, the middle line. The *vav* is the *Kav*, the *etzem* that goes straight down through everything equally: it connects right and left, and that is *v'hanora*, wondrous. *Hagadol*: He is infinite, transcendent. *Hagibor*: He can limit Himself into a limited thing. *Hanora*: He puts the two together until they are *mamash* one. That is the *Kav*: G-d doing whatever He wants.

phrases.he: והב'
phrases.en: and the second thing that we see in the *Kav*,

phrases.he: מה שנקרא בשם קו המדה דוקא,
phrases.en: it's called the measuring line

phrases.he: למדוד כל אורות וכלים כו'
phrases.en: to measure all lights and vessels, to set their limits

phrases.he: וכנזכר לעיל בענין הקו
שנקרא אמת הבנין כו'
phrases.en: it's called like the measuring rod

phrases.he: שזהו היפוך ההתכללות לכאורה.
phrases.en: which is the opposite of *hiskalelus* seemingly,

blocks.text: **And the second thing that we see in the Kav**: **it's called the measuring line**, the *kav hamida*, **to measure all lights and vessels, to set their limits**: here is *chachma*, here is *bina*, and this is where their boundaries are. **It's called like the measuring rod**. **Which is the opposite of hiskalelus seemingly**: it creates distinctions and a system, really false distinctions, since the teacher sees it all as one thing.

blocks.title: Addition and subtraction as separate subjects
blocks.text: For the student's benefit the teacher creates false distinctions, as if addition had nothing to do with subtraction and were a separate subject, to make it simple; to him it is not like that. So seemingly the whole *Kav* is differentiation.

The obvious answer is *hainu hach* (this is that): "If you make the rules, you can break the rules." As with law: that you decide how to interpret the law means there is no law; you are always doing what you want. Setting rules and breaking them look like two things but are both you doing what you want. That is the *Kav*: sometimes G-d wants to make rules, sometimes to break them.

sections.title: Both are true: the Atzmus in the Kav unites, the reshimu in it measures
sections.summary: Because the *Kav* comes from the *Atzmus* before the *tzimtzum*, it can unite every opposite, and for the very same reason it can measure every light, vessel and union: unlimited means able to be as limited as He wants. The *reshimu* in it is the blueprint that makes the world look set, with a *teva*, so that there can be *avoda*.

phrases.he: אך הענין הוא דשניהם אמת
phrases.en: the *inyan* is that they're both true.

phrases.he: ואדרבה
phrases.en: and not only they're both true, on the contrary,

phrases.he: הא בהא תליא
phrases.en: they're interdependent, it's *mamash* one thing,

phrases.he: משום דשרש זה הקו מכח הראשון דעצמיות אור אין סוף שלפני הצמצום הוא בא
phrases.en: So since this *Kav* comes from the *koach* of the *atzmiyus Ein Sof* before the *tzimtzum*,

phrases.he: כנזכר לעיל בענין באורך דוקא נראה אור דקו זה
phrases.en: like we said that it's *davka* from G-d's light that we're seeing the light,

blocks.text: **The inyan is that they're both true.** **And not only they're both true, on the contrary**, **they're interdependent, it's mamash one thing**. **Since this Kav comes from the koach of the atzmiyus Ein Sof before the tzimtzum**, from G-d who is unlimited. As was said, **it's davka from G-d's light that we're seeing the light**: He is really revealing Himself, so there are no limitations and He can do whatever He wants.

phrases.he: ובכח האור העצמות דאין סוף ודאי יש לעשות בחינת התכללות ויחודים של כל ההפכים בכל ההשתלשלות מראש דאדם קדמון כו'
phrases.en: surely the *Atzmus Ein Sof* can connect and unite everything in the whole *hishtalshelus*, it's all one thing.

phrases.he: עד מלכות דאצילות
וכמאמר אנת הוא דמייחד לון ומקשר לון כו',
phrases.en: like it says that You are the one that unites them and ties them together and connects them,

phrases.he: אנת הוא מלגאו ומלבר כו'
phrases.en: You are on the inside and the outside,

phrases.he: וכן ענין שם מ''ה מלגאו דאיהו אורח כל האצילות כו'
phrases.en: this is the *inyan* of the Name *MaH* that's on the *pnimiyus* of the *sefiros*, which is the path that unites *Atzilus*, that is the *Kav*.

phrases.he: וכהאי גוונא
הכל הוא מצד הארת אור העצמות דאין סוף שבקו זה,
phrases.en: that's because the *Kav* is shining with the *or* of the *Atzmus d'Ein Sof*,

phrases.he: שהולך ונמשך עד למטה במלכות, סוף כל דרגין
phrases.en: all the way down to *Malchus*, the lowest levels,

blocks.text: **Surely the Atzmus Ein Sof can connect and unite everything in the whole hishtalshelus, it's all one thing.** As the essence of everything, it transcends all the differences and can make them all get along.

**Like it says that You are the one that unites them and ties them together and connects them**, **You are on the inside and the outside**: to You *pnimiyus* (inner side) and *chitzoniyus* (outer side) are the same. *Davka* G-d's *etzem*, *Ant* (You), can unite everything, because You transcend all limitations.

**This is the inyan of the Name MaH that's on the pnimiyus of the sefiros, which is the path that unites Atzilus, that is the Kav.** The *Kav* is the inner *MaH*, the inner *bittul* (self-nullification), the soul of *Atzilus*: G-d's choice, consciously controlling how everything should be.

**That's because the Kav is shining with the or of the Atzmus d'Ein Sof**, **all the way down to Malchus, the lowest levels**, revealing there that it is not limited, that it is G-d Himself, and breaking all the limitations.

phrases.he: והיא הנותנת דוקא
phrases.en: yet this itself is the reason

phrases.he: שיש בכחו למדוד מדה וגבול לכל אורות וכלים
phrases.en: why He's able to limit and measure everything, set a limitation for everything, in all the lights and vessels,

phrases.he: ולכל יחוד משפיע ומקבל,
phrases.en: in every union between a *mashpia* and *mekabel* it should be *davka* a certain way,

phrases.he: כמה יהיה מ''ד ומ''ן כו'
phrases.en: how much the *mashpia* is going to come to the *mekabel* and how much the *mekabel* is going to have to come up to the *mashpia*.

phrases.he: מצד בחינת הרשימו המגביל לכל אור העצמות באופנים שונים
phrases.en: because of the *reshimu* which limits the light of the *Atzmus* in different ways.

phrases.he: כמו ששיער בעצמות אור אין סוף לפני הצמצום כו'
phrases.en: however He decided in *Atzmus Ein Sof* before the *tzimtzum*.

blocks.text: **Yet this itself is the reason** **why He's able to limit and measure everything, set a limitation for everything, in all the lights and vessels**: **in every union between a mashpia and mekabel** (giver and receiver) **it should be davka a certain way**: how much comes down from the giver and how much the receiver must come up, *MaD and MaN*, *mayin duchrin* and *mayin nukvin* (the male and female waters).

**Because of the reshimu which limits the light of the Atzmus in different ways**: in infinite ways, any way He wants. The *Kav* is G-d choosing which combination to make of the transcendent *gilui* of the *Atzmus Ein Sof* and the limited *gilui* of the *reshimu*, so it is one thing: if He can make it as bright as He wants, He can make it as dark as He wants, **however He decided in Atzmus Ein Sof before the tzimtzum**.

The limitations come from the *reshimu*, all the ways G-d can reveal His light. With the teacher, the explanations in his head are the *reshimu*, and his knowledge, which transcends and unites them, is the *Atzmus* of the light. Measuring it out, he picks explanations and sets up a structure, which is superficial, since he sees how it is all connected and how it could be divided any way. He picks what suits the student, and as they go up the ladder may show them it is more connected, and not so simple.

blocks.title: The Bohr model
blocks.text: At a lower level they make things simple: the Bohr model of the atom, with little balls spinning around. When you get more advanced, they tell you it is nothing like that and far too simple: you cannot point to where the electron is, and it is hardly a thing at all, just an energy field. The real *etzem* of what they understand is not a system; they put a system on it to make it simple, "but it's totally not like that."

blocks.title: Negative numbers
blocks.text: Really no concept is a system. Arithmetic is split into addition and subtraction as if they were opposites, but as soon as you add negative numbers they are the same thing.

phrases.he: ונמצא מצד עצמות האור שבקו נקרא בחינת היולי ליכלל ולחבר את הכל כו',
phrases.en: So it comes out, when we look at the *Kav*, there's two sides you can look at it. From the side of the *Atzmus* of the *or* that's in it, it's a *hiyuli* thing to unite everything.

phrases.he: ומצד כח הרשימו המגביל שבו
phrases.en: but because it's coming from the *reshimu*,

phrases.he: מגביל שיעור ומדה לכל,
phrases.en: to be able to give a limit, and it's able to impose this artificial limitation and order onto everything,

phrases.he: על דרך אותו בחינת השיעור הראשון שנכלל ברשימו זו
phrases.en: however He decided in the *reshimu* how He was going to do it.

phrases.he: על דרך משל אומן
phrases.en: like a *mashal* of a craftsman, like an architect,

phrases.he: העושה רושם, שמגביל האופן של המעשה,
phrases.en: he makes a blueprint for how to make whatever it is,

phrases.he: שיהיה הכל מדוקדק כמו שהוחלט השיעור בעצמו
phrases.en: So now he has this blueprint in order that everything should be built exactly the way that he decided.

phrases.he: שלא ינטה ימין ושמאל כו'
phrases.en: he doesn't want to deviate from his original plan,

blocks.text: **So it comes out, when we look at the Kav, there's two sides you can look at it.** **From the side of the Atzmus of the or that's in it, it's a hiyuli thing to unite everything**. **But because it's coming from the reshimu**, it can **impose this artificial limitation and order onto everything**, **however He decided in the reshimu how He was going to do it**.

blocks.title: The architect's blueprint
blocks.text: **Like a mashal of a craftsman, like an architect**: **he makes a blueprint for how to make whatever it is**, a house, a chair, an *aron kodesh* (a holy ark), a silver *kiddush* cup. The plan comes first, with a little key at the bottom: an inch on the paper means a foot, or ten feet. Then he takes his measuring rod and builds by it. **So now he has this blueprint in order that everything should be built exactly the way that he decided.**

The main thing of the *reshimu*: **he doesn't want to deviate from his original plan**, so he sets it in a blueprint and need not rethink it. In the *nimshal*, it makes the world look set, as if it could not be otherwise: a *teva* (nature).

blocks.title: Name and date in the corner
blocks.text: That gives us the ability of *avoda*. A teacher who wants to put the burden of effort on the students needs a strict system: homework and tests done a certain way, and without the name and the date in the right format, no credit. He does not have to; some teachers are looser and give credit for effort and understanding. But young, immature kids, to work and to feel they accomplish something, need it demanding, and it is only demanding if it has to be a certain way.

blocks.title: You're the teacher, man
blocks.text: He does not really care whether the name is in this corner and the date in that one; he invents the format and makes it the rule, or else it is no good. He is the teacher, so where does this magical rule come from? Yet he presents it as if it were outside his control.

sections.title: Every change comes from the Atzmus: the teacher who leaves his plan
sections.summary: When the light comes beyond the measure of the *Kav*, or less than it, that is only from the *Atzmus*, the one who made the plan and can change it, as only the husband can change the blueprint of the house. Every change in the worlds, from *Shabbos* to *galus*, comes from there, and so we pray to His very *Atzmus* to change even the simple will.

phrases.he: ואף על פי שאם לפעמים יהיה תוספת אור בנאצלים, יתר מכפי מאמר קו המדה כו',
phrases.en: but sometimes G-d breaks the rules, and He makes more of a *gilui* than the way He says it's supposed to be.

phrases.he: היינו מכח האור העצמות דוקא
phrases.en: Has to be *davka* from the *koach haAtzmus*, that He can make it more,

phrases.he: שלפעמים יאיר כך ולפעמים יאיר כך
phrases.en: Sometimes He does it this way, sometimes He does it that way.

blocks.text: But wait: **but sometimes G-d breaks the rules, and He makes more of a gilui than the way He says it's supposed to be**. A *gilui* is supposed to take *avoda*, yet sometimes you get inspired without working: "Sometimes G-d gives you a freebie," an inspiration, *hashgacha pratis*, a miracle.

So what happened to having to do *avoda*? The *kav hamida* in *avoda* is what *HaYom Yom* says of the three kinds of *hisbonenus* (contemplation): without all three steps in order there is no *gilui Elokus* (a revelation of G-dliness); you cannot skip steps. Sometimes G-d gives a little *gilui milmaala* (a revelation from above), but that is special. That is the *Kav*: you go through every step of the *hishtalshelus*, *misbonen* on each as chapter one explained, first *bina*, its length, width and depth, then *chachma* and *Keser*. A whole *avoda*.

Sometimes G-d gives freebies, an inspiration that does not last, not *b'pnimiyus* (inward), as a teacher sometimes makes an exception for somebody. That **has to be davka from the koach haAtzmus, that He can make it more**.

blocks.title: The class trip to NASA
blocks.text: **Sometimes He does it this way, sometimes He does it that way.** As a listener said, the teacher makes a class plan, the *Kav*, what they do each day and in what order; but sometimes he takes them out of it, on a trip to NASA. Little kids learning science do not understand it, but it gives them a wow: there is something way above them, and it motivates them to work to go higher, knowing they could.

So at *krias Yam Suf* (the splitting of the Sea) G-d gave them a *gilui* like *Moshe*'s *nevua* (prophecy), bigger than *Yechezkel*'s, way beyond their level, and at *Matan Torah* (the giving of the Torah) a taste of *Olam HaBa* (the World to Come), as if they were *tzaddikim*: so they would appreciate what they could eventually reach. Then it went back to the plan and they had to do it on their own, knowing there is much more than the way they do it now.

blocks.title: Extra problems and a pop quiz
blocks.text: And when they are bad, as a listener said, he gives them extra problems, or has them sit and do nothing, or springs a pop quiz. What happened to the plan? Because it comes from the *etzem*, the teacher can decide whatever he wants.

Two things. First, he made the rules, so he can break them; he is not stuck in the plan. Second: yesterday he was real nice, today he is mean; which is he? He did not change; it is the same *Kav*. He wants them to understand the subject, so he gives the regular class, something special or a punishment, whatever he measures is good for them, according to the *mekablim* (receivers). The teacher did not become mean; it is the same thing.

phrases.he: ולזה הטעם כל בחינת התחדשות אור באבי''ע, הכל מעצמות אור אין סוף שלפני הצמצום דוקא
phrases.en: this is the reason why any new thing, any change at all in the light of *ABYA*, has to come from *Atzmus Or Ein Sof*, before *tzimtzum*, *davka*.

phrases.he: דהיינו מפני שבאורו העצמי נראה אור בקו זה
phrases.en: because the light that's coming on the *Kav* is coming from G-d's *etzem or*.

phrases.he: לפעמים בתוספת ולפעמים בגרעון
phrases.en: Sometimes it comes more, sometimes it comes less.

blocks.text: **This is the reason why any new thing, any change at all in the light of ABYA, has to come from Atzmus Or Ein Sof, before tzimtzum, davka**: only that has jurisdiction to change the *Kav*, the plan.

Some teachers are robots: once they make a class plan they follow it as if totally stuck in the rules, not human, unreasonable; you could be dying and they won't make an exception. That is a system: once set, you follow it. To change it you have to go to the *etzem*; it has to be a human thing.

sensitivity.reason: Says some teachers are robots who would not make an exception if you were dying: a sneer at a profession.
sensitivity.publishable: Once a class plan is made, it can be followed as if totally stuck in the rules, with no exception. That is a system: once set, you follow it. To change it you have to go to the *etzem*; it has to be a human thing.

blocks.text: So too in the *hishtalshelus*, where if you look there are changes every moment, because it is not really a system. Certainly something obvious, a miracle or a hurricane, has to come from the *Atzmus*.

blocks.title: The architect builds the house himself
blocks.text: **Because the light that's coming on the Kav is coming from G-d's etzem or.** **Sometimes it comes more, sometimes it comes less.** Measured out by a system, it still comes from the *Atzmus*; He decides. The architect himself is building the house from his own blueprint. He can insist that the plan is the plan, or he can say he made the plan and can change it, and build bigger or smaller than it says.

The *asara maamaros* (the ten utterances of creation) are one way to see it. But even *b'etzem* (in itself): the world looks like a system at first, a level that covers over G-dliness; look carefully, with chaos theory for one example, and it is not a system. So it cannot just have been thrown: a conscious volition tells everything what to do every second, as with the body.

blocks.title: A whole world inside of you
blocks.text: Under a microscope the body is a bunch of cells, each like its own organism, trillions of little things living their own lives and running all over the place. Those that move, like blood cells, are like animals; those that stay put but grow, like plants; those that do not move at all, like bone cells, like minerals and stones: "a whole world inside of you." Each has its own *ratzon* and its own brain; it does not know there is a person and does not care. Yet a higher will is imposed on all of them, a *makif* that makes them work together without their knowing it.
blocks.outOfPlace: From the second Q and A tape on chapter 15 (class 48), which reads no line: the world looks like a system, but a will above it makes every change, as lines 37 to 39 say.

blocks.text: The world is like that too. Under a microscope the molecules, atoms and quarks each seem their own little thing, following their own rules by their *teva*. But there is a gap between levels: from the atomic level they should not work together on the molecular level the way they do, or come together into a tree. Going from one level to the next, scientifically the only explanation is an outside *makif* force uniting them. A left kidney cell does not even have the full DNA, only kidney cell DNA; each cell does not know the whole picture, only its own job, and does it as best it can.
blocks.outOfPlace: From the second Q and A tape on chapter 15 (class 48), which reads no line: the world looks like a system, but a will above it makes every change, as lines 37 to 39 say.

blocks.title: The cancer cell
blocks.text: A cancer cell is one that somehow loses its *bittul* to the general thing: the system breaks down, and a kidney cell tries to turn everything into kidney cells, too many, the wrong shape, all wrong.
blocks.outOfPlace: From the second Q and A tape on chapter 15 (class 48), which reads no line: the world looks like a system, but a will above it makes every change, as lines 37 to 39 say.

blocks.title: What keeps the cells in order
blocks.text: What does it? They are not sure yet; when they figure it out, *im yirtzeh Hashem* soon, they should be able to cure cancer and make people live forever. Embryology is already researching what causes this *bittul* over the body: a baby develops very rapidly, yet in the right proportions, order and form. They know chemicals there influence it, mainly a liquid he thinks, but have not isolated what does what. *L'mai nafka mina* (what difference does it make): it is the *tipa* (the drop), with *hei gevuros* and *hei chasadim*; some liquids make it grow, some make it stop, and the right combination makes the right form. Rabbi Walters knew this from *Chassidus* before he researched it in medicine and found them researching it.

blocks.title: Chassidus and the body
blocks.text: It also seems some inhalant would trigger the proper release of these chemicals in an adult, so the body would fix itself up again: as people get older the liquid dries up, the body loses the signals to fix itself, and it deteriorates. It could come through scientific discovery or from learning *Chassidus*: learn *Chassidus* properly and it will do this to your body naturally; medicine might help people before they reach that understanding, maybe not as well. The two will come together: *ruchniyus* (spirituality) is *mamash gashmiyus* (physicality). Science will find it independently on the physical level, but to do it in its real, best form it has to come *davka* through *Chassidus*.

blocks.title: The pool room
blocks.text: A *mashal*: newlyweds are building their house from scratch. The wife comes to look: the foundation is poured, the frame going up, and someone walks her through the blueprint, kitchen, dining room, bedrooms, guest room, and a pool room. She does not want a pool room: make it a guest room or a bigger kitchen, with a *milchig*, *fleishig* and *pareve* island, and a *Pesach* kitchen. The contractor cannot change it and sends her to the boss, and the boss cannot change the blueprint and sends her to the architect.

blocks.title: Sorry lady, go to your husband
blocks.text: The architect sends her to her husband: they agreed on the plan, based on what he wanted, and the architect only drew it up; what is structurally sound he knows, but what goes where he did not decide. The husband wanted a pool room, so much fun; but when she says she would rather have a *Pesach* kitchen, a bigger kitchen or a guest room, he says okay, tells them, and everything changes.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 45 opens by reading the first words of line 40 (w0-5), which the alignment marks only at w1040, and goes straight into this mashal of it.

blocks.text: So to change anything in the *hishtalshelus*, even the smallest *prat* (detail) down in *Asiya*, you have to go all the way up to G-d: nothing in the *hishtalshelus* has the jurisdiction to change anything. Like a phone, whose whole purpose is to give over what you say unchanged, it faithfully gives over what G-d wants. Each level sends you to its boss: up to *Keser*, which comes from the *Malchus* of the world above, on up to the *ratzon kadum* (the preceding will), which comes from the *Kav*. The *Kav* is only the *hiyuli*, with no *pratim*; G-d measures things out for it. So you go to G-d.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 45 opens by reading the first words of line 40 (w0-5), which the alignment marks only at w1040, and goes straight into this mashal of it.

blocks.text: The husband's real *ratzon* is not this room or that; he wants him and his wife to be happy. He thought the pool room would do it; if she would rather have it another way, he makes it another way. His *ratzon*, the *etzem*, stays the same; he measures it out differently. So too when we *daven* (pray), or think of *bitachon* (trust), and ask G-d for a change: He can make the world different and accomplish the same goal. To Him it does not matter, because we asked Him for this.

So we say in *davening* on *Shabbos*: G-d made the world by His *ratzon*, the *ratzon* of the *tzaddikim* and of all the Jews. "It was your fault." You planned it with Him and picked your part: your life, your goal, your challenges. Then you come down and complain, and He thought that is what you wanted. You wanted the challenges; you cannot complain now.

But to change it you have to reveal all the way back to the *etzem* in yourself. As long as you deal on the lower levels you can whine, but that does not mean you really want it different. Be aware of what is really going on, know whether you want it different, then ask, and G-d will change it for you.

So too **the changes in all the faces from Adam Kadmon all the way down to the heel of Adam Kadmon, all the way in Asiya**: like the teacher who sometimes shows a nice face and sometimes a strict one, and punishes.

blocks.title: The field trip and the homework
blocks.text: Like the change from the *Beis HaMikdash* (the Temple) to *galus* (exile). The *Beis HaMikdash* is the teacher's field trip, a reward; *galus* is sitting and doing nothing, or homework, sweating a little, so that those who will not do the *yegia* (toil) on their own are refined by it. So in *galus* we raise much more *MaN* for any little *MaD*, and G-d gives no freebies of *gilui Elokus*.

Before G-d put His *etzem* into the ten *sefiros* as a *chafetz chesed* (one who desires kindness), we can ask Him to change the *ratzon* and stop being one: when the goyim are being mean to us, we ask Him to be a *chafetz gevura* instead.

**We ask Him to change the whole hashara, the whole plan of how He had it all measured out all the way down to Asiya to come in a different way**, **like we ask Him to go from din to chesed** (from judgement to kindness), as on *Rosh HaShana*: You planned it the hard way; make it the nice way. Or the other way: give it to our enemies.

sections.summary: Even the essential *middos* in the *Atzmus* are not the Essence, which is not stuck in being a *chafetz chesed*, so a request can change the will without changing Him. Prayer is therefore to Him and not to His *middos*: not a sob story that plays on His nature, but a request for a kindness He does not owe.

blocks.text: The text says the end of *os hei*; it should be *os tes* (section 9): **like we explained at the end of tes about that I am G-d, I do not change**, between a *ratzon* of *chesed* and of *din* in the first light, before the *tzimtzum*.

**Like we explained in os yud**: the *etzem* is the same. The husband changing the room is no real change, only in how it is measured out; he just wants them to be happy. The teacher, strict or nice, is the same guy with the same *etzem ratzon*; and even if he changed the *ratzon* he would be the same guy, since the whole *ratzon* is just him. As section 10 said, the *etzem* is higher than being a *chafetz chesed*: it has that ability, but it is not stuck in it.

From the side of the *etzem*, it does not have to come out *davka* one way; He makes all these *tzimtzumim* (contractions) before it does. So when you ask Him to change it, nothing essential is at stake. First, He does not have to be a nice guy. Second, a nice guy can want it different ways: he need not want to give this one shoes; it depends on the situation. And once you know what you want, you can have different plans to do it. Each level can change without affecting the higher ones, **like explained at length in os yud-alef**.

blocks.text: **And when we say you should daven to G-d and not to His middos**, it means **even His middos ha'atzmiyim** (His essential attributes): not that G-d is essentially a nice guy, so give Him a sob story and He will give you what you want.

blocks.title: The sob story
blocks.text: Give a person a sob story because you think he is nice and will feel bad for you, and he knows you are being manipulative; instead of *chesed* he will *davka* do the opposite, because you are not recognizing him. Playing on someone's nature, with reverse psychology or a sob story, is like taking his hand, reaching it into his pocket and making it hand you the money from his wallet. You treat him as a piece of meat, a very big insult, "and you deserve to get punched in the face."

That is not recognizing G-d. So they *daven* for a *chesed chinam* (an unearned kindness): I realize You do not have to do it, and nothing I can do can make You do it; I am asking You sincerely for a favor. That brings out the *ratzon*, but you have to recognize the *etzem*.

**Because really the Atzmus Ein Sof is not affected in any of these middos really. It's really higher than that.** **This is what we say that You connect them all, You unite all the sefiros**: *Ant*, **davka G-d Himself, His etzem**; **You are one, but not the cheshbon of the ten sefiros**. Being above them all and not stuck, He can unite them: to Him the limitations do not exist.

Then He was *metzamtzem* His *etzem* to reveal it in different ways, like masks and tools. They all come from His *etzem* and are really one: He is the kind guy, and He is the mean guy. *Ant hu*. The kindness and the meanness look different only to you.

That is section 11: if *chesed* goes all the way up to the *etzem* and *gevura* too, they are one *etzem*, not two things. Being mean and being nice, as a listener puts it, is Him doing whatever He wants. There is no real thing of being kind: you make a pattern that defines kind, but you are doing what you think best. Like addition and subtraction, they look opposite and are not.

blocks.title: Head souls and foot souls
blocks.text: So with all the Jews: in the *pnimiyus* they are the same, though they come out as head souls, hand souls, heart souls and feet souls, with different jobs, and they can hate each other. The head guy says the main thing is *hisbonenus* to understand *Chassidus*, and hates going on *mivtzoim* (outreach campaigns); the foot guy says the main thing is *mivtzoim*, and hates learning *Chassidus*. Each thinks the other contradicts him, and really each is using his *koach* to serve G-d as best he can.

sections.title: Two equal, infinite lines: the Kav as a measuring stick for the Essence's will
sections.summary: In the *Atzmus*, the power to hide and limit and the power to spread and unite are two lines, equal and both infinite, and so they stay equal when they come down in the *Kav*: every change, from weekday to *Shabbos*, is one power showing as *chesed* and *gevura*. The *Kav* is a *hiyuli* like a measuring stick, and any exception shows that the system is only His choice.

blocks.text: **So too, from etzem Ein Sof comes the koach hagvul v'hamida** (the power of limit and measure), in the *reshimu* in the *Kav*, **and because of this reshimu it's called kav hamida**: G-d chose that it be a certain way. **And they're interdependent**: G-d can do what He wants, so He can make a system and break a system.

**Like explains elsewhere about the inyan of chesed and gevura in the Atzmus of the Ein Sof**: first **the koach hagvul, the gevura, which is that He's able to limit and hide within Himself higher and higher to no end, His etzem or**, making it look like a *reshimu*, separate, limited and totally set.

blocks.title: Shake the lulav; the wall says no
blocks.text: In the light you see an inner *nekuda* uniting it, a *kavana* (intention). In the *reshimu* there are no deeper meanings: all He wants is that you take a *lulav*, with the *hadassim*, *aravos* and *esrog*, and shake it, and that is it. Or you try to walk through a wall and the wall says no, "no whys, no buts, that's just the way it is": the magical word *teva*. Really that comes from the *Atzmus*: a *metzius* on its own, with no reason before or after it, the *yesh gamur* that comes from the *yesh amiti*.

**That's the Ein Sof that goes up to no end**, **and there's also hispashtus ha'or down to no end**: **that through the Kav it comes down through the reshimu and G-d reveals Himself in the world more and more**.

blocks.title: The Rebbe's sichos
blocks.text: Which side is *chesed* and which *gevura*? It does not matter: they are interchangeable, as your right side faces another's left, a totally relative term. When the Rebbe comes out with lots of *sichos* (talks), that is a *chesed*: he teaches us a lot. But for him it is a really big *gevura*: instead of learning on his level he has to come down to this really stupid level and talk really slowly and stupidly, for hours, and when they do not get it, do it again.

sensitivity.reason: Says the Rebbe has to "talk really slow, and really stupidly" to us; meant of the listeners' level, but it could read as disrespect for the Rebbe.
sensitivity.publishable: Which side is *chesed* and which *gevura*? It does not matter: they are interchangeable, as your right side faces another's left, a totally relative term. When the Rebbe comes out with lots of *sichos* (talks), that is a *chesed*: he teaches us a lot. But for him it is a really big *gevura*: instead of learning on his level he has to come down to our level and talk slowly and simply, for hours, and when they do not get it, do it again.

blocks.title: The Rebbe's locked room
blocks.text: When the Rebbe locks himself in his room and does not come out for a long time, that is a big *chesed* for him, like a vacation: things on his level, much more *b'gilui* to him. To us it is a big *gevura*; we do not appreciate it. Rabbi Walters thinks that is why the Mitteler Rebbe does not say here which is *chesed* and which *gevura*: it is explained both ways.

That is what is explained here: the names and the system are superimposed. It makes it easier to start learning *Chassidus*: they draw you a map, *Atzilus*, *Beriya*, *Yetzira* and *Asiya*, the ten *sefiros* in three lines, tangible enough to memorize and feel you understand something. But it is totally *maalim* (concealing), a *masach* that is *mavdil* (a screen that separates), covering over the *etzem*, and it leads to crazy ideas, as if it were a machine.

Explain the thing itself and people understand it much more easily. That is why people keep asking how one place contradicts another: they do not get that it is not this system. Even *chesed* and *gevura* are relative and interchangeable, superimposed, and the distinctions are not true. Yet there is truth to them: "It's not like totally bogus. It's not totally true, either." It is like a person who decides to do things in a system: the system itself is a choice, so it is not really a system. It is both at once.

blocks.text: **These two lines, these two abilities are exactly equal**, *shekulin*: **they're both completely infinite, equally infinite**. G-d can transcend everything infinitely, above all levels, above even the ten *sefiros* of *Yachid*, above *Atzmus*: "If you can name it, He can go above it." And it is just as infinite going down.

Since in the *Atzmus* the two are equal, G-d is *kol yachol* both ways equally: He can transcend everything, and He can limit Himself to the smallest thing and put His whole *etzem* there, and to Him it is the same. In the *Kav* these two *middos* come out in a limited way, according to the *mekablim*, yet they stay equal: the *Kav* measures things as big or as small as G-d wants, **to either limit and divide and separate, or to connect and unite**.

**And so too all the changes in the light and the hamshacha**, **whether it's coming more or less**, **like change from the week to Shabbos and Yom Tov**, with their different *yichudim* (unions), and from the *Beis HaMikdash* to *galus*: **it's all really one power, which is equal**, **which is revealed in two opposite ways**: making the rules and breaking them.

So what is the difference between the week and *Shabbos*? In the week G-d makes a system, and you follow it and are *mevarer* (refine) things; on *Shabbos* He reveals that we are above the system. The *etzem* is above either and can choose either: it transcends everything and goes into everything, two ways of revealing the same *etzem*. *Shabbos* within the week, and what in *Shabbos* comes from the week, shows the *yichud* of the two.
**They both come from the koach and the first or of the Atzmus Ein Sof**, **as it is essentially to itself**: since essentially it is, *kaviyachol* (as it were), both ways, the *Kav* reveals both.

blocks.title: The measuring stick does not limit the house
blocks.text: **This is like we explained before**, in section 14: **the Kav is a hiyuli compared to the rest of the hishtalshelus, which is like the shetach** (the area), **according to the etzem hamashpia that he can bring out the shetach however he wants**. A measuring stick does not limit the house: keep measuring, and make it as big or as small as you want.

blocks.title: The teacher's compromise
blocks.text: **Just that in your etzem it's in a much bigger way, the ability that you have.** **But when it comes on the Kav**, **now the same thing is coming out in a limited way**. The teacher understands the idea infinitely both ways: he sees the one *nekuda* that transcends all explanations and includes every *inyan*, and he can also spread it into infinite separate explanations and *meshalim*, each its own *inyan*. But when *b'poel mamash* (actually) he explains it to a student, he makes a compromise, infinite neither way, from the same source, now according to the *mekabel*.

**Therefore both the tzimtzum and hispashtus, the Kav is really coming from there.** So he can be *maarich* (extend) the *inyan* back to the *etzem* with someone on his level, or bring it down to a little kid, and it is all the same. G-d reveals *tzimtzum* and *hispashtus*, *chesed* and *gevura*, in the *hishtalshelus* only in a limited way, but it comes from the *etzem*: He can do whatever He wants.

We usually see G-d doing what He wants only a little, within the ten *sefiros*, a little more, a little less. But any change shows He is above the whole system. Whoever says he keeps the laws and the system and is only making a little exception is wrong: "once you make a little exception, that's really revealing that the whole thing is bogus": no system, no rules, no limits.

Even in a store, when the person says he does not have the jurisdiction and you have to go to his manager, it is not really true: he is a person, and he could make an exception. Maybe he is afraid of getting in trouble, but he could. A cashier at Walmart could really do whatever they want; they are human, though they sometimes forget it.

blocks.text: And why is a manager any better? He is not; they just set up a system where he is allowed and this person is not. It is only a judgment call, and I could make the same one; maybe I am more qualified and smarter. But part of what you decide is that he is in charge and I am not, and you listen to the orders: "the system is only that you decided to make a system." *V'dai l'mevin*.

reviewQuestions.question: If the *reshimu* holds G-d's whole *etzem*, why does a rock, a tree or ink on paper show nothing of Him by itself, and where is He seen instead?
How can G-d "decide to be a squirrel" without being trapped in it, and why does that make bowing to a thing *avoda zara*?
What two opposite things are found in the *Kav*, and why is "if you make the rules, you can break the rules" the answer?
Why, in the *mashal* of the newlyweds' house, does every request end with the husband, and what does that teach about change in the *hishtalshelus*?
Why should one *daven* to G-d and not to His *middos*, and what is wrong with a sob story?
In what sense are the two lines of limiting and spreading "equal", and how does the difference between the week and *Shabbos* show it?
